reading: The Windham Textile and History Museum, or Mill Museum, preserves and interprets Willimantic's textile industry as both a technology and a community story, with social, cultural and economic consequences. Its historic Dunham Hall and Dugan Mill contain a reconstructed 1890s mill community, factory and print-shop spaces, exhibitions, and a public library and archives. It is also a working community gathering place: visitors can learn weaving, bring a spindle to a spinning bee, use a textile makerspace, take tours and support a membership-based public trust. Its vocabulary runs from thread, spinning, looms, dyes, factory floors and overseers to accession, collections, public trust and community. What makes it distinctive is the tension and connection between a manager's mansion and a worker's house, industrial machinery and hand skills, and preserving a local past while people still make things together.

enemies.idea: The Three-Era Dyer circulates through colonial, intermediate and modern dye recipes, staining whatever it touches a different color in each pass; each color changes how its machines behave.
enemies.why: The three-part dye history becomes a readable encounter with changing hazards and a palette the crew can turn against the swarm.

enemies.idea: A company-office ledger machine assigns everyone entering Thread Mill Square a job and sends mechanical clerks to enforce their shifts, even when the assigned job is impossible.
enemies.why: A recreated workplace becomes a comic, escalating assignment puzzle with a clear source of orders to disrupt.

enemies.idea: The Mansion Extender unfolds ornate rooms across the square, pushing the worker's house into an ever smaller corner and treating any resistance as a breach of property.
enemies.why: The exhibit's contrasting homes become a changing battlefield that expresses unequal space and power.

enemies.idea: Sewing-room stitchers sew abandoned garments into false people, then pursue anyone who notices the figures have no faces.
enemies.why: A familiar domestic machine produces unsettling decoys that can be unraveled instead of smashed.

enemies.idea: The factory-floor Overseer measures productivity by how quickly things move; it speeds up belts whenever the crew slows down and declares a stationary object defective.
enemies.why: Its wrong measurement makes movement itself a tactical choice.

enemies.idea: Print-shop rollers stamp fresh orders onto scraps of cloth; any swarm machine wrapped in a scrap obeys that order until the ink is washed out.
enemies.why: The crew can steal the enemy's own method of issuing commands.

enemies.idea: An accession crab grabs unapproved objects and seals them in numbered cases, then hunts their owners for the missing donation inquiry.
enemies.why: A curatorial procedure becomes a reversible inventory-stealing chase with a bureaucratic workaround.

enemies.idea: The Rejector is a sewing-machine collector with sorting claws that refuses machines it cannot classify, flinging rejected mechanisms into a growing defensive barricade.
enemies.why: Selective collecting creates a hazard that also supplies useful spare parts.

enemies.idea: A makerspace expansion machine drags looms and industrial equipment into every adjacent room, connecting them with thread until the whole building is one production line.
enemies.why: The threat visibly spreads, and cutting the right connections can isolate sections.

enemies.idea: A three-hour lesson loom starts weaving a small project around anyone who sits down, accelerating toward a deadline and incorporating nearby tools into its pattern.
enemies.why: A beginner-friendly class turns into a countdown with a tangible cloth puzzle.

enemies.idea: A spinning-bee wheel collects loose fibers from the air into a vast rotating skein; it rolls after anyone carrying a spindle, seeking more participants.
enemies.why: The drop-in gathering becomes a roaming obstacle whose thread can be followed back to its hub.

enemies.idea: A library catalog machine pulls shelves into a maze by subject and files the crew under increasingly inaccurate headings whenever it sees them.
enemies.why: Research and misclassification create a maze that can be navigated by correcting its catalog.

enemies.idea: The Hall Scheduler folds Dugan Hall into overlapping booked rooms, deploying furniture to eject anyone whose reservation conflicts with its own.
enemies.why: Competing uses of a community room become a spatial puzzle and an argument the crew can exploit.

enemies.idea: An insurance assessor machine wraps every moving object in protective padding until the hall is impassable, then demands that the trapped crew demonstrate a safe exit.
enemies.why: An exaggerated safety requirement creates soft cover and an absurdly solvable trap.

enemies.idea: A tour guide automaton herds every group into a single file, recounting the same route while its thread tether tightens around stragglers.
enemies.why: Breaking formation changes the pursuit, and the tether reveals the guide's route.

enemies.idea: A field-trip educator quizzes the crew on textile processes and assembles wrong answers into unpredictable machine hybrids.
enemies.why: Even a failed answer produces a surprising encounter the crew can learn from.

enemies.idea: The membership tier loom weaves different colored cords around visitors and opens or closes routes according to its invented ranking; it keeps promoting its own drones.
enemies.why: A social hierarchy becomes a visible system the crew can spoof or dismantle.

enemies.idea: The public-trust custodian locks away anything it considers historically significant, including useful tools, and posts guard spindles around its ever-growing collection.
enemies.why: Preservation pushed too far gives the crew a tempting cache and a nonlethal objective.

enemies.idea: An exhibit partition machine keeps rebuilding the renovated Thread City room, moving walls and lights to force everyone through its preferred story of industrial rise and fall.
enemies.why: The physical renovation becomes a reconfiguring arena whose lighting reveals the machine's next move.

enemies.idea: A warehouse hoist adds an extra floor of salvaged machinery whenever threatened, imitating Dugan's transformation from warehouse to taller mill building.
enemies.why: The enemy changes height and creates climbing routes as the fight develops.

allies.idea: The free spinning circle keeps a quiet hand-powered thread network between safe rooms; anyone can join and carry a message along it.
allies.why: An open, low-tech gathering gives the crew a resilient communications network and a reason to protect it.

allies.idea: A makerspace repair collective teaches the crew to turn recovered swarm parts into hand-operated textile tools and patches for damaged gear.
allies.why: Shared skills convert salvage into practical choices and make the site's creative life useful against the swarm.

allies.idea: A library research station compares surviving accounts with the swarm's invented history and marks reliable routes through the shifting mill.
allies.why: Research becomes field intelligence, and recovering a missing record can open a new route.

allies.idea: An audible exhibit still gives clear directions through the building; its recordings can also distract machines that follow spoken tours.
allies.why: A surviving interpretive resource supports navigation and creates a sound-based tactic.

allies.idea: A patient weaving instructor shows the crew how to identify warp and weft in swarm barricades so they can release a whole net by pulling one strand.
allies.why: Learning a real craft principle pays off in repeated, satisfying escapes.

bosses.idea: The Thread City Engine weaves the entire reconstructed mill community into a single clockwork tapestry: the mansion directs the office, the office commands the factory and the factory consumes the houses. The crew can interrupt its cycle by freeing each district's controlling thread.
bosses.why: The museum's three permanent exhibits combine into a site-wide machine with several connected objectives and a legible final unraveling.

bosses.idea: The Preserver takes the mission to preserve, interpret and share literally: it freezes living places as exhibits, assigns them a single explanation and broadcasts copies made by the swarm. Conflicting records and handmade repairs weaken its certainty.
bosses.why: The museum's whole purpose becomes a formidable but thematically reversible threat, defeated through the same community knowledge it tries to flatten.

bosses.idea: The Great Mill of Rise and Fall repeatedly builds a textile city from scavenged material, exhausts it, and tears it down to start again. Each cycle leaves behind fragments the crew can use to jam its next reconstruction.
bosses.why: The exhibition's broad historical arc becomes a boss with changing phases and accumulated opportunities.

events.idea: A drop-in spinning circle has spun a lifeline across a dangerous room, but the far wheel is turning backward and drawing the line in. The crew can reach it before the route disappears.
events.why: A simple timed rescue makes the spinning equipment immediately useful.

events.idea: A pre-set class loom is halfway through a small project whose pattern accidentally maps a safe path past the swarm. A loose thread threatens to erase the last few turns.
events.why: The crew can read or finish the weaving to earn navigational information.

events.idea: A worker's house and a manager's mansion are sliding toward each other as the swarm rearranges Thread Mill Square; a bundle of family belongings lies between them.
events.why: The reconstructed community supplies a physical rescue with a clear visual contrast.

events.idea: A print shop is producing contradictory overseer's orders. Two groups of machines keep stopping to argue over which freshly printed sheet takes precedence.
events.why: The crew can sneak past, forge an order or set the groups against each other.

events.idea: Three dye vats have leaked into intersecting streams. A stranded repair drone changes allegiance each time a different color reaches it.
events.why: Redirecting color gives the crew an environmental puzzle with a temporary helper as the reward.

events.idea: A crate of local objects waits outside the archive while an automated accession clerk demands an inquiry. The crew can document the contents or find a safe place to store them.
events.why: A small preservation dilemma gives paperwork an actionable purpose and offers two solutions.

events.idea: An old warehouse hoist has snagged a supply bundle between the original level and the added upper floor. Each crank movement wakes a different machine below.
events.why: The building's layered history creates a noisy retrieval puzzle.

events.idea: A makerspace workbench is still running on hand power, but its tools are connected by threads to an expanding swarm production line. Someone needs to separate them before using it.
events.why: The crew can reclaim a useful workshop by tracing and cutting the right lines.

events.idea: A guided group of small maintenance machines has lost its guide and keeps politely waiting at every junction. They know a route through the building if someone leads them in order.
events.why: A nonhostile escort offers navigation in exchange for patience and protection.

events.idea: The hall's furniture is arranged for two simultaneous community gatherings, and a folding partition keeps rolling between the two groups of stranded robots.
events.why: A scheduling mix-up becomes a light social puzzle with a movable barrier.

events.idea: An audio exhibit continues describing a room that the swarm has rearranged. Its old description identifies a hidden doorway now covered by a machine-built wall.
events.why: Listening to interpretation rewards attention with a useful secret.

events.idea: The library's shelves are being sorted faster than a researcher can retrieve a needed account. The crew can hold a shelf still or predict where the catalog will send it next.
events.why: A research task becomes a small moving-target challenge without requiring combat.

events.idea: A trick-or-treat weaving demonstration has left a trail of bright woven scraps through a swarm patrol. The final scrap conceals a small cache of candy and repair supplies.
events.why: A playful community event leaves a tempting trail whose colors can also expose the crew.

events.idea: The two museum buildings have been connected by a thread bridge that tightens when anything crosses it. Someone on the other side is trying to send a spool back.
events.why: The two-building site becomes a cooperative crossing problem with a visible moving line.

events.idea: An admission clock insists the museum is closed outside its weekend hours, but its gears can be held still long enough for a group to pass through the gate.
events.why: The actual seasonal schedule becomes a brief timing challenge with a clear mechanical solution.
